text.headline: Timeline of Bosnia and Herzegovina
text.text: Major events in the history of Bosnia and Herzegovina.

events.headline: Early Settlements
events.text: The area now known as Bosnia and Herzegovina was inhabited by Illyrian tribes. These tribes established various settlements and cultures throughout the region.

events.headline: Roman Conquest
events.text: The Romans conquered the region and incorporated it into the province of Illyricum. This brought significant cultural and economic changes.

events.headline: Division of the Roman Empire
events.text: The Roman Empire was divided into Eastern and Western halves, with Bosnia and Herzegovina falling under the Eastern Roman Empire (Byzantium).

events.headline: Fall of the Western Roman Empire
events.text: The Western Roman Empire fell, leading to increased influence of the Byzantine Empire in the region.

events.headline: Formation of the Banate of Bosnia
events.text: The Banate of Bosnia was established, marking the beginning of a distinct Bosnian state. It was ruled by the Ban Kulin, who promoted trade and cultural development.

events.headline: Bosnia Becomes a Kingdom
events.text: Bosnia was elevated to a kingdom under the rule of Tvrtko I, marking a significant step in its political development.

events.headline: Ottoman Conquest
events.text: The Ottoman Empire conquered Bosnia, leading to significant demographic and cultural changes, including the spread of Islam.

events.headline: Austro-Hungarian Occupation
events.text: Following the Congress of Berlin, Bosnia and Herzegovina was occupied by Austria-Hungary, leading to modernization but also rising nationalist sentiments.

events.headline: Assassination of Archduke Franz Ferdinand
events.text: The assassination of Archduke Franz Ferdinand in Sarajevo triggered World War I, highlighting Bosnia's geopolitical significance.

events.headline: Formation of the Kingdom of Serbs, Croats, and Slovenes
events.text: After World War I, Bosnia and Herzegovina became part of the newly formed Kingdom of Serbs, Croats, and Slovenes, later known as Yugoslavia.

events.headline: Axis Invasion of Yugoslavia
events.text: Nazi Germany and its allies invaded Yugoslavia, leading to significant suffering and the rise of resistance movements in Bosnia.

events.headline: Formation of Socialist Yugoslavia
events.text: After World War II, Bosnia and Herzegovina became one of the six republics of the Socialist Federal Republic of Yugoslavia under Josip Broz Tito.

events.headline: Independence Referendum
events.text: Bosnia and Herzegovina held a referendum for independence from Yugoslavia, which was largely supported by the Bosniak and Croat populations.

events.headline: Start of the Bosnian War
events.text: The Bosnian War began shortly after independence, marked by ethnic conflict and significant humanitarian crises.

events.headline: Dayton Agreement
events.text: The Dayton Agreement was signed, effectively ending the Bosnian War and establishing the framework for the current political structure of Bosnia and Herzegovina.

events.headline: Constitutional Changes
events.text: Bosnia and Herzegovina underwent constitutional changes to improve governance and address issues stemming from the Dayton Agreement.

events.headline: European Union Membership Application
events.text: Bosnia and Herzegovina submitted its application for EU membership, marking a significant step towards European integration.

events.headline: Centenary of World War I
events.text: Bosnia and Herzegovina commemorated the centenary of the assassination of Archduke Franz Ferdinand, reflecting on its complex history.

events.headline: Political Crisis
events.text: Bosnia and Herzegovina faced a political crisis marked by ethnic tensions and challenges to the governance structure established by the Dayton Agreement.

events.headline: Continued EU Integration Efforts
events.text: Bosnia and Herzegovina continues its efforts to meet the criteria for EU membership, focusing on reforms and addressing political challenges.
